title: Evidence Of No Culprit
paragraphs: Itsuki half-closed his eyes at my words.
“What is it? Strength is justice, you know?”
“…It was a mistake on my part to consult you about this. That’s right, Motoyasu-san, you’re someone who believes everything can be solved with power.”
“Oh? Have I failed to persuade you?”
“That said… there may be people out there who can only be saved by someone like you, Motoyasu-san.”
Itsuki stroked Kou’s throat and then smiled.
“I suppose so.”
“I’ll say it as many times as necessary—strength is justice.”

Itsuki believes that justice is about being fair, helping the weak, and crushing evil. But my justice is different. The righteous ones are the Filolials and Father. Anyone who becomes Father’s enemy is evil. I stand by Father and will eradicate all his enemies. In other words, fighting for those you believe in is justice—it is loyalty.

“Conflict arises when neither side is willing to compromise or when unreasonable demands are made without any intent to back down. The reason we failed to persuade Naofumi-san last time—or rather, the reason we failed in all the worlds you’ve experienced, Motoyasu-san—is because we weren’t willing to compromise. We refused to listen.”
“That seems to be the case.”
“No matter how much you concede, you can’t persuade someone who refuses to listen from the start.”
“Like sharing enhancement methods or explaining the reasons for battle?”
“Exactly… If you decide from the outset that the other person is evil, you’ll never be able to hear them out.”
Itsuki nodded repeatedly, as if he had reached an epiphany. His expression was different from before—like he had been freed from something that had been weighing him down.
“I understand now. Listening to what you had to say, Motoyasu-san, I kept wondering—just how selfish and villainous have I been? But at the same time, I didn’t want to believe it.”
“We’ve fought many times, haven’t we, Itsuki?”
“Yes, both the previous loop and the one before that.”
“And each time, you were weak.”
Well, that was because he hadn’t been able to properly implement enhancement methods.
“If I don’t start with the assumption that no one is purely evil, like in fiction, then I’ll just end up playing the role of a self-righteous hero.”

In the first world, too, Itsuki clashed with Father multiple times. When I heard that Father had kidnapped Fiancée, I immediately assumed he was the villain. Well, back then, I was no different. Itsuki just seems to have a harder time breaking free from that way of thinking.
“You know how detective characters appear in mystery novels?”
“Detectives?”
“Yeah. I’ve only seen them in dramas and manga, but they always seem like hunters closing in on their prey.”
“I am the Love Hunter!”

“…That was so stupid it threw me off, but I’ll continue. Those kinds of detectives usually go, ‘This person is the culprit. But I don’t have proof yet. So, let’s find evidence to corner them.’ Right?”
“Now that you mention it, that does seem to be the case.”

“I don’t mean to criticize detective stories or anything. But from now on, I want to take a different approach: ‘This person is not the culprit. But there is a culprit. I need to gather all the evidence—not just to prove this person’s innocence, but to make sure that no one in this group is the culprit.’ …Though, maybe that’s just wishful thinking.”
“Hmm, you’re thinking about some rather troublesome matters, aren’t you?”
“That being said, I can’t say I don’t understand what you mean.”
“I’ve seen cases of false accusations in the news many times before coming to this world.”
“If those in charge of making arrests were to think that way, perhaps the world would become a better place.”
“Though, as Itsuki says, it’s probably not that simple.”

“Rather than simply assuming that only the people we’re protecting are innocent, perhaps the quickest path is to consider that the other party might also be innocent. Justice is only served when the charges are solidified, and even then, action should only be taken once there is no evidence left to prove innocence.”
“Looks like Itsuki is deep in thought about this as well.”
“You have quite a troublesome personality, don’t you?”
“If we just threatened the culprit with this spear, they’d confess easily.”
“And even if they didn’t succumb to force, illusions would make things simple.”
“But still…”
“This time, Itsuki is surprisingly willing to believe what I say.”
“That’s because you’ve given me undeniable facts, Motoyasu-san. Also, I hadn’t yet reached my own certainty.”
“Strike while the iron is hot—Father would say that, wouldn’t he?”

“That’s exactly right… In that sense, all the past loops must have had meaning. And through our journeys, I’ve come to understand that you, Motoyasu-san, along with Naofumi-san and Ren-san, are not bad people.”
“Itsuki gazed off into the distance.”
“Did he just realize something?”
“I don’t want to be deceived by those who wear the guise of the weak… I want to believe in all of you.”
“As he said that, his back looked strangely pure to me.”
“Oh? That over there is—”
“After taking a brief look around town, we made our way back toward the guild.”
“There, Father and the others were waiting for us.”
“Ren and Yuki-chan were already present as well.”
“Welcome back, Motoyasu-kun, Itsuki.”
“I have returned!”
“How was it?”
“It seemed like a relatively peaceful town.”
“Indeed.”
“It wasn’t exactly a tour of the town, but we did find a vigilante outpost… They were ignoring adventurers who were asking for help.”
“Itsuki pointed at a building on the other side of the main street, across from the guild.”
“I was worried Itsuki might step in.”
“Well, if he had, I would have dealt with it.”
“A well-placed Paralysis Lance would have taken care of the issue.”
“Honestly, I personally wouldn’t want to ignore that either…”
“Seeing this, Father and Ren both muttered something about how corruption is everywhere.”
“When we asked what happened, they said someone had their wallet stolen by a pickpocket.”
“Ugh… It sounds like it’ll be tough to identify the culprit.”
“Yeah, there wasn’t much we could do about it, so all we could do was sympathize… By the way, where’s Kou?”
“Anticipating something like this, I had Kou track the culprit by scent.”
At the same time I said that, Kou returned. A loud, thudding noise echoed.
“I’m back!”
“Waaahhh!”
Kou had grabbed the culprit by the collar with his beak and dragged them over.
“W-What the hell is this talking monster?! Is it yours?!”
“Yes. You’re a pickpocket, aren’t you?”
Itsuki patted the culprit down, pulling out multiple wallets and interrogating them.
“N-No! These are my wallets!”
“Is that so? Then why don’t you tell the vigilante corps at the outpost the same thing?”
“You sicced a monster on me, and now you’re acting all righteous?!”
“…That’s a fair point. Kou, why this person?”
“The scent~ I followed this person’s scent, and it led me right to them~ So I caught them~”
Kou’s words were slightly muffled. Well, that’s only natural, considering he was holding the culprit in her beak.
“The scent, huh…”
“Aren’t they still arguing with the vigilante corps?”
As I pointed toward the outpost, the pickpocket suddenly started struggling.
“We should avoid making too much of a scene. Motoyasu-san often says I lie a lot, but dealing with this is troublesome. Let’s just say we were almost pickpocketed ourselves and hand them over.”
Taking Kou with him, Itsuki headed toward the vigilante corps’ outpost. Before long, he returned, having turned in the thief.
“The evidence was undeniable. The victimized adventurer was shocked to find their wallet again. The culprit kept trying to paint us as the real criminals and played the victim, though.”
“Well, at least you caught the thief, right?”
“Motoyasu says I used to lie a lot, but in some situations, I suppose it’s unavoidable.”
“That said… if I make a habit of doing this, I might really end up lying all the time.”
“But calling ourselves Heroes and declaring that we’ll hunt down thieves would be dangerous right now.”
“Yeah. At worst, we could end up dragging this whole town into something dangerous.”
“…That’s true. But I’ll be careful. If I keep handling things this way, I might lose the ability to tell the truth when it really matters.”
“You’re really serious about this, huh?”
“…It’s not that I’m serious. It’s that my sense of justice is so strong that I lose sight of my own position. When it’s convenient, I want to push a lie through.”
His response is different from how he used to be.
“At the very least, I’ll make an effort not to deceive my comrades.”
“Well, for now, isn’t this fine? You caught the culprit. In the end, someone was helped. You should just be happy about that.”
Ren crossed his arms as he spoke. He sure sounds self-important.
“You got a heartfelt ‘thank you’ from that adventurer, didn’t you? That’s good enough.”
“You’re overthinking it. Were they lying about being robbed?”

“…No. If we hadn’t caught the pickpocket, no one would’ve gotten that wallet back. If the adventurer had already been at the outpost by the time we turned the thief in, I might have been suspicious, but…”
“Exactly. You helped someone, so just be happy about it.”
“…Alright.”
As I turned to look, the adventurer bowed deeply in gratitude, and Itsuki gave them a small wave in response.
Hmm… Regardless of the complexities, it seems like we did a good thing.
Since I’ve made all sorts of promises to Filo-tan, I’ll keep doing my best for true peace! I can’t afford to lose to Itsuki!
“If… if we hadn’t found any evidence, I might have considered forcing a confession.”
